requirements.quote:
This example shows the logical authentication process that starts
   from the a configured root DNSKEY (or DS RR) and moves down the tree
   to authenticate the desired "example" DNSKEY RR.  Note that the
   logical order is presented for clarity.  An implementation may choose
   to construct the authentication as referrals are received or to
   construct the authentication chain only after all RRsets have been
   obtained, or in any other combination it sees fit.  The example here
   demonstrates only the logical process and does not dictate any
   implementation rules.
requirements.condition: When an implementation constructs the authentication chain.
requirements.required_behavior: An implementation may choose to construct authentication as referrals are received, only after all RRsets have been obtained, or in any other combination it sees fit.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's authentication-chain scheduling can be inspected to identify its permitted strategy; the example does not impose a particular construction order or require support for every strategy.
